title: Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, fourth edition — reviewed periodization passages
authors: G. Gregory Haff, Chapter 21; G. Gregory Haff and N. Travis Triplett, editors; NSCA
type: Foundational textbook · selected programming passages reviewed
population: General strength and conditioning; the chapter annual-plan example concerns a collegiate basketball athlete, not professional baseball.
access: Paid textbook. Cited by chapter and page; no text, tables or figures are reproduced.
findings: Defines periodization and programming hierarchy, describes annual-season organization and short-term variation, and discusses contrasting model terminology and mixed comparison findings. Supports original planning and critical-appraisal exercises.
limitations: Historical textbook synthesis, not a current systematic review or evidence of an optimal professional-baseball model. The course does not adopt generic peak-duration limits, fixed recovery periods, automatic phase doses, categorical overtraining claims or source sample schedules as prescriptions. New cases, numbers, graphics and assignments are original.
locations: Chapter 21, p. 600 (printed p. 584): central concepts and definition; reviewed for conceptual organization, not categorical physiological predictions.
Chapter 21, pp. 603–604 (printed pp. 587–588): periodization hierarchy and periods.
Chapter 21, pp. 608–609 (printed pp. 592–593): seasonal organization and undulating versus linear terminology, including conflicting comparative findings.
Chapter 21, pp. 610–611 (printed pp. 594–595): scope of the illustrative basketball annual plan, joint planning and limits of generalization.
license: Copyrighted textbook, cited only. Hub text and graphics are newly written.
reviewed: 2026-10-13: selected full passages read; not a complete textbook review or a new systematic evidence review.

title: The use of yank-time signal as an alternative to identify kinematic events and define phases in human countermovement jumping
authors: Sofyan B. Sahrom, Jodie C. Wilkie, Kazunori Nosaka, Anthony J. Blazevich
population: 32 physically active healthy adult men; activity ranged from recreational exercise to international running-based sport. Not a professional-baseball cohort.
access: Full open article XML verified through the official Europe PMC repository; selected methods read. The direct PMC webpage returned a verification page.
findings: Provides a documented example of acquisition, processing and event definition in CMJ analysis. Used for a concise methods comparison rather than a device prescription.
limitations: Study-specific acquisition and processing. It does not establish a universal sample rate, filter setting, baseball readiness threshold or equivalence across devices. The course mechanical calculations and diagrams are original synthetic teaching exercises.
locations: Sections3.1–3.2: signal processing and force-derived kinematics.
license: CC BY4.0 as stated by the journal; original figures and study data are not reproduced.

title: Intraclass correlation – A discussion and demonstration of basic features
authors: David Liljequist, Britt Elfving, Kirsti Skavberg Roaldsen
type: Methodological research · theory and Monte Carlo simulation
population: Statistical models and simulations with a clinical illustration; no baseball cohort.
access: Full open text verified at PLOS and through Europe PMC; selected theory/reporting sections read.
findings: Explains variance dependence and why consistency and absolute agreement can differ when systematic shifts occur.
limitations: The article centers on single-score ICC and proposes a particular analytical approach. It does not validate a baseball test or replace a design-specific statistical analysis. The course does not adopt every procedural recommendation or give categorical ICC quality thresholds.
locations: Sections2.1–2.5: measurement matrix, variance models, agreement and consistency.
Sections4–7: simulations, interpretation and reporting discussion.
license: CC BY as stated by PLOS; no source figures, tables or datasets reproduced.

title: A Guideline of Selecting and Reporting Intraclass Correlation Coefficients for Reliability Research
authors: Terry K. Koo, Mae Y. Li
population: Clinical reliability methodology; no baseball-specific sample.
access: Abstract and publicly indexed Model, Type and Definition Selection sections verified. Direct PMC page returned a verification page and full XML was unavailable; complete article not reviewed in this session.
findings: Supports a concise ICC reporting checklist specifying model, score type, agreement definition, software and confidence interval.
limitations: Only the selected accessible sections support the checklist. Generic qualitative ICC cutoffs are not adopted as universal practical standards. No detailed unseen content is attributed to this source.
locations: How to Select the Correct ICC Form: Model Selection, Type Selection, Definition Selection; selected publicly indexed text.
license: Publisher copyright; link and brief original paraphrase only.
reviewed: 2026-10-13: abstract and selected indexed sections only
